Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) machines work by using a very strong magnetic field to align the magnetic properties of atoms in your body, and radio waves to disrupt this alignment. When the alignment is restored, signals are emitted called resonances, which are detected by the machine and converted into images. There is no ionising radiation involved, and MRIs are particularly useful in imaging the brain and spinal cord.
